correctness.rationale: Exactly 11,394 matching faces and 55,280 Hasse incidences are constructed from 24 graph edges. A 5,673-pair matching is proven acyclic by exhaustive DAG sorting. The reduced critical cells are two in degree three and 23 each in degrees four/five. Reconstructed signed Morse matrices D4 (2x23) and D5 (23x23) compose to zero and have unit Smith invariant factors 1^2 and 1^19; an explicit unimodular 2x2 minor of D4 gives the first CW cancellations. Since the initial skeleta are 2-connected and later 3-connected, Hurewicz and primitive attaching maps permit integral 3/4 and 4/5 cancellations, leaving two S4 and four S5. The independent mod-two simplicial boundary computation agrees. A separate exact initial-family computation confirms no earlier Möbius ladder has homology in two degrees. All computations and certificates were replayed from new actual package paths.

originality.rationale: The fully accessible original Agarwal–Basak paper settles vertex-independence and perfect-matching complexes, not the strictly larger ordinary matching complex. Published index checks for graph aliases, line graphs, Betti ranks and nearby ladder families found no equivalent or stronger explicit classification. The closest M8, M10 and Möbius–Kantor results do not imply the M16 statement. Revised manuscript full-text and unindexed stronger results remain residual risks; the check is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: This is the first size in the canonical Möbius-ladder family for which ordinary matching homology occurs in two positive degrees; sizes four through fourteen are verified to have only one. The mixed integral homotopy decomposition therefore marks a concrete boundary for proposed periodic classification, rather than an arbitrary graph slice. It also distinguishes the full matching complex from the previously studied perfect matching complex of the very same graph; the latter consists of only two 3-spheres, while the former is 3-connected with higher-dimensional nonzero homology. Exact homotopy and integral attaching information supply a meaningful complete finite benchmark.
